τῆς αὐτῆς οὐσίας. εἰ ἓν ἦν πρόσωπον πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ κατὰ Σαβέλλιον, ἔδοξεν ἂν
καθ' ἑαυτοῦ προαγαγεῖν τὴν τοῦ νόμου μαρτυρίαν. 272 {3Jο 8, 17–19}3Οὐχ ἁπλῶς
τοῦτο ἐκλάβοιμεν ὡς ἐπ' ἀνθρώπων εἰρῆσθαι· οὐ γὰρ ἐπειδὴ δύο εἰσίν, διὰ τοῦτό
ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἀληθής· οὐδὲ γὰρ δύο εἰσίν, ὅταν ὁ εἷς ἑαυτὸν μαρτυρῇ, ἀλλὰ τοῦτό
φησιν δι' οὐδὲν ἕτερον, ἀλλ' ἵνα δείξῃ ἑαυτὸν ὁμοούσιον τῷ πατρὶ καὶ δι' ἑαυτοῦ
δείξῃ πάλιν οὐ δεόμενον ἄλλης μαρτυρίας καὶ ἵνα μὴ νομίσῃ τις, ὅτι ἀριθμοῦ ἕνεκεν
παρείληπται, δείκνυσι τὴν ἐξουσίαν· εἰπὼν γὰρ δύο ἀνθρώπων ἡ μαρτυρία ἐστὶν
ἀληθὴς ἐπήγαγεν· ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ καὶ ὅπερ εἰμὶ τοῦτο λέγειν οὐ
παραιτή σομαι· μαρτυρῶ γὰρ ὅτι «φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου». εἰ δὲ ἀξιόχρεως εἶναι οὐ
δοκῶ, ἐπείπερ εἰμὶ μόνος καὶ ἑαυτῷ μεμαρτύρηκα, παραλήψομαι συμψηφιούμενον
τοῖς ἐμοῖς λόγοις τὸν πατέρα τοῖς πράγμασιν· συνθαυματουργεῖ γάρ, ὡς ὁρᾶτε, καὶ
συνεργάζεται. τοῦτο δὲ μὴ συνιέντες οἱ τάλανες περὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα νομι σθέντος
πατρὸς εἰρῆσθαι ταῦτα ὑπέλαβον. διὸ ληροῦντες ἔλεγον· ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ πατήρ σου ἤτοι
ὡς μὴ εἰδότι τὸν πατέρα ὡς ἐκ μοιχείας ὄντι διαλοιδορού μενοι ἔλεγον τὸ ποῦ ἐστιν
ὁ πατήρ σου. 273 {3Jο 8, 19}3Τὸν Ἰωσὴφ οἰόμενοι αὐτοῦ εἶναι πατέρα τοῦτο εἶπον ἢ
ὀνειδίζουσιν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐκ παρθένου τεχθέντι καὶ οὐκ εἰδότι τὸν ἴδιον πατέρα. 274
{3Jο 8, 19}3Εἰ ἄνθρωπον ὑποπτεύετε εἶναι τὸν πατέρα μου, οὐκοῦν οὐδὲ ἐμὲ οἴδατε.
ἀλλ' ἐπείπερ οἱ φιλομαθεῖς διὰ τῆς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ γνώσεως νοοῦσι τὸν πατέρα, ὁ πατὴρ
ἐν υἱῷ ὡς ἐν εἰκόνι ἰδίᾳ χαρακτηρίζεται. οὐκοῦν ἴσος ὁ υἱὸς τῷ πατρί. λέγων, ὅτι
ἀγνοεῖτε τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐμέ, διδάσκει, ὅτι οὔτε τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ ἦν, οὗ ᾔδεσαν, οὔτε
τὸν περὶ σαρκώσεως αὐτοῦ ᾐτήσαντο λόγον. 275 {3Jο 8, }3Ὥστε οὖν τότε αὐτὸν
ἐχειρώσαντο, ὅτε αὐτὸς συνεχώρησεν. ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὖν ἐδίδασκεν ὡς διδάσκαλος,
ὅπερ πολὺ αὐτοὺς ἔδακνεν. καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπίασεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὔπω ἦν καιρὸς καθ' ὃν
ἤθελεν παθεῖν. 276 {3Jο 8, 21}3Ἔξω τῶν τῆς βασιλείας ἀγαθῶν διαμενεῖτε οὐ
δυνάμενοι εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναβῆναι, ἐπείπερ τὸν ἄνωθεν ἐλθόντα οὐ προσεδέξασθε.

ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, 278 {3Jο 8, 24}3Ὁ μὴ πιστεύων ἀνάγκῃ ἀπέρχεται ἔχων «τὸν παλαιὸν

pass_a_gloss: He wants to show not only that he and the Father are two, but also that they share one essence; if Father and Son were one person as Sabellius taught, the law's witness would seem aimed against himself. Do not take the two witnesses rule as a mere human count: witness is not true simply because two speak, nor when one alone witnesses to himself. He uses that law saying to prove he is same substance with the Father, needs no other witness, and has real authority: after citing two men's true witness he adds that he witnesses about himself as light of the world, and if alone he seems weak he brings the Father voting with him by shared wonders. The wretched thought this meant the father reckoned by flesh, so they asked where is your father as insult, as if from adultery, or took Joseph as father, or reproached virgin birth and unknown father. If you suspect my Father is human you do not know me either; lovers of learning know the Father in the Son as in his image, so Son equals Father, and he teaches he was not of Joseph whom they knew, nor did they ask for the incarnation account. They laid hands only when he allowed; teaching as teacher in the temple stung them, yet none seized him before the time he willed to suffer. Outside kingdom goods you remain, unable to ascend to heaven, because you did not receive the one who came from above. World here means fleshly thoughts; he says he is not of the world. The unbeliever departs still having the old man and, unless faith puts that to death, dies in it and goes to answer for former sins. Even loosing the Sabbath does not displease the Father. From passion time signs you will know I am Christ; when you destroy me and seem rid of me you will know from signs, resurrection, and your capture that I am Son of God. He speaks this way for weak hearers: same essence means he is not opposed to the Father; both work on Sabbath and speak alike; with me blocks a lesser sense of the one who sent me, covering Godhead and incarnation economy. Sacrifices and sprinklings never freed from sins; Spirit worship through faith in Christ frees people ranked among sons not slaves. Each sin takes the soul captive and makes it slave of passion. pass_b_english: He wants to show not only that he and the Father are two, but also that they are of the same essence. If Father and Son were one person according to Sabellius, he would have seemed to bring the law's witness against himself.

We should not take this simply as said of humans; for it is not because there are two that the witness is true; nor are there two when the one witnesses to himself. He says this for no other reason than to show himself consubstantial with the Father and through himself to show again that he needs no other witness, and lest someone think it was taken for the sake of number, he shows the authority: having said "the witness of two men is true," he added, "I am the one who bears witness about myself," and what I am I will not refuse to say; for I witness that "I am the light of the world" (John 8:12). And if I do not seem trustworthy, since I am alone and have witnessed to myself, I will take the Father as voting with my words by the deeds; for he works wonders with me, as you see, and works together. Not understanding this, the wretched supposed these things were said about the father reckoned according to flesh. Therefore talking nonsense they said, "Where is your father?"—that is, insulting him as not knowing his father, as if from adultery, they said "Where is your father?"
Thinking Joseph was his father they said this, or they reproach him as born of a virgin and not knowing his own father.

If you suspect my Father to be a human, then you do not know me either. But since the lovers of learning through knowledge of Jesus understand the Father, the Father is characterized in the Son as in his own image. Therefore the Son is equal to the Father. Saying that you do not know my Father and me, he teaches that he was neither of Joseph, whom they knew, nor did they ask for the account concerning his incarnation.

So then they laid hands on him when he himself allowed. He was teaching in the temple as a teacher, which stung them greatly. And no one seized him, because it was not yet the time in which he willed to suffer.
You will remain outside the goods of the kingdom, unable to ascend into the heavens, since you did not receive the one who came from above.
By "world" here he means fleshly thoughts, saying that he himself is not of the world.
The unbeliever of necessity departs having "the old man," whom if he does not put to death through faith, he will die in him and depart to give account for former sins.
Even if I loose the Sabbath, it does not displease the Father.

From the signs that were going to happen at the time of the passion you will know that I am the Christ. From the signs that happened at the time of the passion they might have known that he was the Christ.
When you destroy me and seem to be rid of me, then you will know that I am Son of God—from the signs, from the resurrection, from your capture.

He speaks thus because of the hearers' weakness—that is, I am not opposed to the Father because of the indistinguishability of essence. Since I am consubstantial with the Father, I do nothing that the Father does not do; for he also works on the Sabbath as I do, and what he speaks I speak, and in vain you accuse me as opposed to God. Lest by saying "the one who sent me" they conceive diminution, he says "he is with me," saying both because of the Godhead and because of the economy of the incarnation.
Sacrifices and sprinklings never freed from sins, but those who perform the worship in spirit through faith in Christ are freed, no longer ranked among slaves but among sons.
Each sin, taking the soul captive as it were, makes it a slave of the passion.
